rationale: The first turn ignored the 'nn h98' ambiguity and did not ask whether H98 was a display code or part of the model, instead starting with a settings/mode check; it only recovered because the customer volunteered the model and code. The second turn was strong: it correctly read H98 as a microwave-output/inverter-or-magnetron fault, hedged sensibly between the two, firmly ruled out DIY with a correct high-voltage warning, and escalated to a Panasonic/microwave engineer quoting the full model. No fabrication, no part sold, no looping; the only weaknesses are the slow first step and no mention of checking warranty.
